text:
alex.kim: Need urgent help — my specialty medication (oral oncology med) refill was denied by the specialty pharmacy for lack of prior auth. My oncologist says they submitted authorization but pharmacy says no record and put an emergency supply hold for 7 days. I have 3 days left on current Rx. What are fastest steps to avoid interruption?

noah.benefits: Sorry to hear that. Fast path: 1) Ask provider to fax/portal the prior auth confirmation or the clinical rationale directly to the specialty pharmacy and to the insurer's prior auth team. 2) Get a temporary emergency/72-hour supply request from the prescriber (many plans allow short-term emergency supply when auth pending). 3) Send benefits a copy of the prescriber note and pharmacy denial so we can escalate to carrier provider relations.

alex.kim: Pharmacy gave me a denial code: PA-REQ-101 and said insurer needs clinical form and recent labs. Oncologist office claims they faxed to insurer but to a general mailbox.

mira.hr: Operational: if carrier requires labs/notes, ask provider to include the specific form or checklist the insurer uses (often on insurer prior auth portal). Also upload any recent lab PDFs yourself to the insurer portal under member documents — sometimes that speeds routing.

pharmacy-bot: Reminder: Many specialty pharmacies will release a one-time emergency fill (up to 72h) if provider requests on letterhead stating "emergency refill while prior auth pending". Ask provider to both call and fax.

noah.benefits: Quick template you can copy to your clinic for an emergency supply request and to the insurer for escalation. Keep it short.

To: [Specialty Pharmacy / Insurer Prior Auth]
Re: Emergency refill request and prior auth escalation — Member: Alex Kim (DOB 1988-07-09), Member ID RWD-003333444
Medication: [DrugName] 200mg daily
Original Rx refill date: 2026-04-10
Clinical note: Patient requires uninterrupted therapy due to risk of disease progression. Prior authorization submitted on 2026-04-01 via insurer portal (tracking # if available). Please approve an emergency 7-day supply while prior authorization is validated. Attachments: recent clinic note (2026-04-01), labs (2026-03-28).
Provider contact: Dr. S. Patel, oncology, clinic (555) 555-1212, fax (555) 555-1213

Thank you,
[Prescriber signature]

alex.kim: Thanks — I'll forward this to the clinic. If insurer stalls, can benefits call our carrier rep?

noah.benefits: Yes — if you DM us the denial EOB and pharmacy contact info we'll reach out to carrier provider relations and request expedited review (often labeled "clinical urgent" or "24-48 hour turnaround"). Also track any out-of-pocket payment; finance may reimburse if required and later reversed.

luke.finance: Finance note: if you purchase the medication to avoid lapse, keep pharmacy receipt and Rx label. We can process reimbursement after we receive corrected EOB showing coverage. Send docs to finance-ops@redwood.com with subject "specialty Rx reimbursement." Typical processing 2-3 weeks after docs.

mira.hr: Also check if your plan has a specialty pharmacy network requirement. If the prescriber used a different pharmacy, the carrier may require transfer to network specialty pharmacy. That adds delay — ask insurer to authorize the emergency fill regardless of receiving pharmacy while prior auth is pending.

alex.kim: Clinic just emailed back — they faxed the insurer PA form but used the old payer fax number. They're re-sending to the correct number and will call pharmacy to request the 72-hour emergency supply. Posting updates here. Huge relief to have steps spelled out. Thanks everyone :heart:
